name: Participatory democracy
summary: Participatory democracy holds that citizens should take a direct and continuing part in the decisions that affect their lives, not only vote for representatives. It sees participation as educative, building the capacities of citizens, and extends it from government to workplaces, communities and schools. Most adherents combine direct mechanisms such as assemblies, referendums and participatory budgeting with representative institutions.
scope: The modern participatory-democracy tradition as the scholarship defines it: a model that extends citizens' direct, continuing part in decisions from government to the economy, workplaces and communities, and holds that participation educates citizens ('the best school of citizenship', Decidim volume, s6; Dixon, s5). Its canon is Rousseau as forerunner, Carole Pateman's Participation and Democratic Theory (1970), Benjamin Barber's Strong Democracy (1984), Arnstein's ladder of citizen participation (1969) and the New Left's Port Huron Statement (1962), which Gemmell (s7) says coined the term. It excludes deliberative-democracy theory in its own right and direct-democracy purism, which the sources set against it (s6), and the 1960s New Left's wider policy positions on race, war and corporations.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Port Huron, 'Values' (economic sphere): 'the economic experience is so personally decisive that the individual must share in its full determination' and the economy's 'major resources and means of production should be open to democratic participation'. Decidim, section 2.1 (participatory democracy as a model of society), says that unlike liberal representative democracy, where 'democracy stops at the gates of the factory', participatory democracy extends participation 'starting with politics and the economy' (citing Pateman 1970).

reviewHistory.rationale: Pateman sees industry as the most important site of democratic education and stresses democratising its authority structures; Port Huron opens production to democratic participation.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should help decide how a public budget is spent, through open meetings or votes.
missingStatements.rationale: Participatory budgeting, begun in Porto Alegre in 1989, is presented as a signature participatory mechanism.

missingStatements.text: Citizens chosen by lot should be convened to deliberate and advise on major public questions.
missingStatements.rationale: Citizens' assemblies such as Ireland's 2011 assembly and France's 2019 climate convention are cited as participatory instruments.

missingStatements.text: Taking part in public decisions develops citizens' abilities and sense of responsibility.
missingStatements.rationale: The Decidim volume calls participation 'the best school of citizenry', a leitmotif of the participatory tradition from Rousseau to Pateman.

notes: Strands differ: Pateman and the New Left emphasise workplace and community self-management, Fishkin and Landemore emphasise deliberation, and some adherents favour referendums while others doubt them. Port Huron's policy positions on race, war and corporations belong to the 1960s New Left rather than to participatory theory as such. Later pass 2026-11-25: answers rest on Port Huron's values section (full text, Wayback copy), Decidim (Barandiaran et al. 2024), Dixon, Gemmell, the Elliott 2026 and Wolfe 1985 abstracts and Pateman 2012. Themes searched: participation and the economy, workplace and unions, direct votes, referendum, recall, sortition, delegation, transparency, violence, elections, experts, leadership, representation. Most statements stay null because those sources state no position on them; Port Huron's policy sections (race, war, corporations) are the 1960s New Left's positions, outside the scope.
